## Strategy guide

**Source:** SCPT episode 458, “The Ultimate Guide to the Titans of Ul,” published 2026-05-27. Complete, checksum-verified ASR transcript; speaker identity is not claimed. The episode mixes Prophecy of Kings-era faction knowledge with an early Thunders Edge breakthrough discussion. These are strategic opinions and reported interactions, not a current-rules or errata review. The `Slumber State Computing` passages especially describe early research/playtest games.

### Strategic thesis

Titans convert exploration into a durable board network. Saturn Engine II supplies inexpensive reach and a credible fleet, while sleepers and Hel-Titans create structures, defense, production, and future access. This makes Titans unusually flexible at stage-one scoring, control objectives, and many structure requirements. The constraint is command-token income: ships, activations, and deployments all compete for the same pool. Draft influence, sell Terraform when opening money changes a real action, and keep the cruiser upgrade moving toward round two. (C01, C02, C08, C09, C10)

### Opening economy and map

**Influence is the first slice question.** The speakers want influence in the slice because Titans have many useful activations and their cruisers each occupy fleet capacity. One speaker says a 0-resource/8-influence slice is workable; the 7-resource/3-influence alternative feels worse because Elysium can supply resources while command tokens remain the limiting input. This is a preference, not a universal map formula: planet access, skips, objectives, and neighbors still matter. A tech skip is valuable for reaching the upgrade and later technology choices. The speakers disagree about how much blue technology deserves priority, while agreeing that yellow/green routes fit Titans well. (C01, C09, C24)

**Terraform is opening liquidity.** It adds one resource, one influence, and all three planet traits to a non-home, non-Mecatol planet. One speaker prefers selling early, usually asking around three trade goods and adjusting to the buyer; the other supports getting immediate value when it enables the desired tech, Warfare build, or round-one score. Raise the ask when an attachment or four-of-a-kind objective makes the note unusually valuable. Waiting can improve its objective value, so do not treat three trade goods as a fixed market price. A Jol-Nar Research Agreement exchange can be better when Titans receive useful technology, with Hyper Metabolism specifically praised; this is one of the few swaps the speakers elevate over a cash sale. (C02, C03)

A useful opening goal is to score a feasible public objective in round one, then pursue Mecatol Rex. The ideal is to score, take Politics, and take Custodians; if that cannot be arranged, the speakers prefer scoring on tempo and targeting an Imperial bonus point in round two over sacrificing the opening score for a speculative Custodians grab. Imperial can be taken after another player reaches Mecatol. The recommendation depends on objective feasibility, speaker order, and the opponent's approach: Saar is named as a potential Mecatol contest, though a heavy Saar push can leave other systems open to Titans' cruisers. (C20)

### Build the engine

**Saturn Engine II is the essential upgrade.** The guide describes it as a cost-two cruiser with combat six, movement three, capacity two, and sustain damage. That package gives Titans an unusually cheap all-purpose ship for reaching objectives, the Fracture, and fights. Prioritize obtaining it early, ideally by round two; the exact technology route should flex with skips, breakthrough access, and strategy-card timing. The speakers acknowledge its limits: it uses fleet capacity, has less carrying potential than carrier-heavy fleets, and lacks bombardment. It is versatile rather than best at every specialized task. (C08, C09, C24)

Tech primary is not an automatic first pick. The speakers rank Leadership and Trade higher, with Politics also high when it secures speaker and the round-two plan. Technology sits in the middle: primary or secondary can accelerate Saturn Engine II, but an early Warfare pop may leave no useful Warfare secondary to follow. Leadership is especially valuable because tokens fuel Titans' multiple activations and deployments. Trade helps a two-commodity faction pay for its opening. Diplomacy is lower priority unless a spend objective, refresh, or breakthrough timing makes it directly useful. Construction is usually low priority because sleepers can become structures, though the primary can solve an infantry shortage or enable extra opening fleets. (C21, C22)

The speakers recommend considering a Warfare opening when a nearby three-planet system creates a strong sleeper and structure line. It can create a staging position for expansion and accelerate the commander unlock. Remember the distinction they stress: Warfare creates the activation opportunity, but sleepers placed then are awakened on a later activation, not during that same action. Construction may instead be useful where its build and the Hecatoncheires deployment add enough ground forces to take more planets. (C19, C22, C23)

### Sleeper timing and board presence

Plan Scan Link, Terragenesis, and Awaken as separate timing windows. Scan Link explores one planet in the activated system only if a Titans unit was already there. After exploring a planet without a sleeper, Terragenesis can place or move one. Awaken is available when activating a system that already contains a sleeper; the guide emphasizes that the sleeper must predate that activation. In practical terms, explore and place now, then awaken on a later activation. The speakers warn that the printed timing is easy to misread. (C04, C05)

An unredeemed sleeper can be valuable. Opponents see it and must consider that Titans may later activate the system and turn it into a Hel-Titan. Coalescence makes this a real projection threat when another player enters: Titans can awaken into the contested area and participate in combat. The speakers say they once underrated this option and now see it as a defining skill. The five-sleeper limit means placement still requires selectivity; this is deterrence and future access, not guaranteed control of the planet. (C06, C07)

Spread Hel-Titans across planets when the goal is broad defense and production. Their structure/ground presence, shield, sustain, and production make planets harder to take and help with structure objectives. Multiple Hel-Titans in a system can be useful for production, but concentrating several on one planet often projects less power than distributing them. Keep one Hecatoncheires in reinforcements when possible: when a qualifying PDS is placed, the mech's deploy effect can add a mech and infantry instead. The guide describes using Transit Diodes to remove and place PDS as a way to trigger this elsewhere. Its rules discussion also cautions that Hell-Titans cannot be moved by effects that merely move ground forces; verify exact interactions before relying on them. (C10, C11, C26)

### Economy, leaders, and negotiations

Titans' commander, Tungstantus, rewards actual production with a trade good. The guide notes that a Hel-Titan's production can generate that good in the same production window, allowing it to fund the current build. The speaker also describes spending it immediately to avoid Mentak pillage. This and the unlock condition of five structures can make early Hel-Titan placement pay twice: toward the commander and future production income. A three-planet system can accelerate the unlock, but starting infantry, planet access, and deals may leave Titans one short. (C13, C19)

The hero refreshes Elysium and increases its values. The speakers disagree about whether the added resources or influence are usually more important. They often favor influence because tokens are the binding constraint; spend for resources when a concrete tech, objective, or double-tech plan makes it worthwhile. (C12, C14)

Terraform and coalescence create bargaining options. Trade Terraform for immediate money or a useful alliance; the episode names Arborec, Cabal, Naaz-Rokha, Crimson, and Jol-Nar as alliances with particular appeal in different situations. The early Slumber State Computing discussion adds possible deals involving shared defense, an alliance swap, objective progress, trade refreshes, and action-card draws. These examples came from a small number of research games, and the speaker openly questions whether some were good trades. Make the exchange specific and price each side's benefit; consent and trust are necessary. (C02, C03, C16)

Be especially cautious about helping Yssaril coexist under the breakthrough. The speakers worry that repeated status-phase card value could give Yssaril a major advantage; they doubt ordinary payments compensate for that risk. Conversely, the breakthrough can support Push Boundaries when Titans coexist on planets whose owner retains control, but this is presented as conditional, early-era advice. Do not confuse preparing a scoring position with meeting an objective: check the revealed requirement and the actual board state before claiming the point. (C15, C17, C28)

Tellurian, the agent, is described as a flexible hit cancel rather than ordinary sustain damage. Preserve it for an important round-two fight or a late game contest; once it no longer protects Titans' own path, it can be used to disrupt an opponent. The timing and target should be chosen for the actual win condition. (C18)

### Late game and counters

The Fracture is a natural Saturn Engine II destination. Three movement can carry the cruiser through the ingress, across the Fracture, and into the adjacent system, opening routes to relics and other slices. A Fracture-adjacent ingress in the home slice can also serve as a staging or production position. The speakers rank the Imperial bonus and public scoring ahead of relic hunting in round two; take relics when those priorities are covered. Hel-Titans need special positioning or Transit Diodes for some Fracture plans, while the cruisers provide more straightforward access. (C26, C27)

Titans can pivot toward many control and structure objectives, and the breakthrough discussion adds possible coexistence-based lines. The speakers call out stage-two structures as especially comfortable and describe a possible Rule Distant Lands setup. Treat those as options to evaluate, not automatic scores. Make an Example is singled out as more awkward because it can require building destroyers, while opponents with large carrier fleets or ground-force volume can test Saturn Engine II's limited capacity. X-89 is proposed as a late-game answer to a ground-force mismatch; Fleet Logistics remains useful for an action-phase win, so the choice depends on what the table demands and whether both routes are realistically affordable in tech. (C09, C15, C25, C28)

### Evidence limits

This is an ASR-based paraphrase of one complete episode, not speaker-attributed testimony or rules research. The source itself labels compatibility “not reviewed; publication date is not a ruleset guarantee.” POK-era faction advice and Thunders Edge-era breakthrough comments are mixed. Slumber State Computing is treated as early playtest discussion, and no breakthrough ID is supplied because it is unresolved in the assigned component reference; its claims therefore remain component-unlinked in JSON. Proper nouns and a few named interactions are ASR-sensitive. Current errata, exact component text, variant rules, and engine legality remain unverified. (C15–C17, C24–C28)

## Combined source guidance

The guide above contains conditional, transcript-cited advice. The pinned documents below add community research and a bot-oriented mid/late-game profile. Their ordered technology/build lists are proposals, not unconditional policy targets. Keep source disagreements and expansion assumptions visible.

**Historical scope:** upstream statements about available factions, engine support, bot behavior and benchmark results describe that source revision; they are not checks of this checkout. Podcast timestamps in upstream notes are approximate and do not share the local transcript verification.

> Historical source excerpt; advice and engine claims retain the source’s assumptions.

* Versatile; Saturn Engine II all-rounder; sleepers give structures without Construction;
  weakness is influence/tokens (each Saturn Engine is a fleet token) (458 1:40).
* **Plan (very confident):** score every round from R1; either take custodians or be second to
  Rex and take Imperial R2; only Saar out-muscles them at Rex (458 1:46).
* R1: Leadership medium-high, Politics top if also scoring, Trade high, Warfare strong (no
  token, sleepers redeemable same round), Technology middling (but reach Saturn Engine II by
  R2), Construction/Diplomacy low (458 1:54-2:12).
* Tech: Saturn Engine II then **X-89** ("the finisher"); Bio-Stims, Transit Diodes, Integrated
  Economy on the way; AI Dev/Psychoarchaeology to reach Saturn II fast; Sling Relay below
  average; prefer X-89 over Fleet Logistics if only one (458 2:14-2:24).

</details>

<details><summary>upstream-community — The Titans of Ul (`titans`)</summary>

[Exact pinned section](../sources/upstream-community.md#the-titans-of-ul-titans) · [Repository source](https://github.com/Feelx234/TI4-Bot-Dev/blob/1fd3092ad83a72bc3e379ac3946852b409adee6d/crates/ti4-server/docs/COMMUNITY_FACTION_STRATEGIES.md#the-titans-of-ul-titans)

> Historical source excerpt; advice and engine claims retain the source’s assumptions.

**Engine check.** Home Elysium 4/1; start 1 dreadnought, 2 cruisers, 2 fighters, 3 infantry, dock;
starting techs Antimass Deflectors and Scanlink Drone Network; 2 commodities. Saturn Engine
cruisers (move 2, capacity 1; II: combat 6, move 3, capacity 2, sustain; GYR). Hel-Titan PDS
(ground force and structure, sustain, space cannon 6, PRODUCTION 1). Terragenesis: after
exploring a planet, place a sleeper token. Awaken: activating a system with sleepers turns them
into PDS. Commander (5 structures): a trade good each time you produce. Hero: Elysium +3/+3 and a
space cannon battery. Mech replaces a PDS placement with a mech and an infantry.

**Play.** A "foothold" faction: secure a slice with a path to Mecatol Rex; Saturn Engine II is the
first technology priority (3 cruisers with mechs and infantry are a cheap strike force); Hel-Titans
(the best defensive ground unit, mini-factories) hold the slice; the commander makes production a
trade-good engine. Reactivating explored systems awakens sleepers, so Warfare in round 1 suits
Titans (re-activate to awaken and produce). Disagreement: secure the slice first versus grab the
equidistant at once (the sleeper makes it hard to take back) and take Mecatol Rex early in round 2
([BGG Titans of Ul Guide, 2023](https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/3103032);
[BGG 2021](https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/2641111);
[r/ti "How to play Titans in this slice", 2025](https://www.reddit.com/r/twilightimperium/comments/1lmrak1/how_to_play_titans_in_this_slice/)).
Round 1 cards: Trade (x-1 deals), Technology, Warfare, Construction. Traps: cruisers fall off
mid-game without a bigger fleet; awakening costs command tokens. Sell Terraform for 3-4 trade
goods (it can carry an objective). Titans trivially score structure and attachment objectives.

**Strength.** A in both 2025 lists, row 3 in SCPT 2022; early-PoK data called them strong.

**Bot feasibility.**
- Awaken: activating a system with own sleepers is worth a PDS per sleeper; `activation_value`
  should add that value (the engine applies Awaken on activation). Value high, effort S-M.
- Terragenesis prompt: always place a sleeper on the explored planet. Effort S.
- Research: Saturn Engine II (GYR; Scanlink Drone Network is the yellow, so AI Development for the
  red, then a green technology or skip),
  Hel-Titan II only for unit-upgrade objectives. Effort S.
- Build mix: Saturn Engines as transports and warships. Check that capacity-1 cruisers count as
  transports in the opening production rule (same as Argent). Effort S.
- Objective focus: structure objectives; Construction primary always takes a PDS (Titans' PDS are
  ground forces too). Effort S.

</details>

## Strategy connections

- [Terragenesis](../components.md#ability-terragenesis) **requires** [Awaken](../components.md#ability-awaken). The token placement from Terragenesis must occur on a prior action if Awaken is to redeem that sleeper; it cannot be created and redeemed during the same activation. Sources: [SCPT 458, 2022.10–2100.32s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/458-the-ultimate-guide-to-the-titans-of-ul/)
- [Coalescence](../components.md#ability-coalescence) **enables** [Hel-Titan I](../components.md#unit-titans-pds). A sleeper can remain dormant as a threat and be converted to a Hel-Titan when later awakened into a contested location, subject to combat. Sources: [SCPT 458, 2172.88–2204.40s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/458-the-ultimate-guide-to-the-titans-of-ul/)
- [Saturn Engine II](../components.md#unit-titans-cruiser2) **scores** [Push Boundaries](../components.md#public-objective-push-boundaries). Cruiser mobility and capacity can help Titans control enough planets; breakthrough coexistence is a separate conditional scoring avenue. Sources: [SCPT 458, 5710.60–5726.12s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/458-the-ultimate-guide-to-the-titans-of-ul/)
- [Hel-Titan I](../components.md#unit-titans-pds) **enables** [Hecatoncheires](../components.md#unit-titans-mech). When placing a PDS on a planet with a mech available in reinforcements, the described deploy ability may substitute a mech and infantry. Sources: [SCPT 458, 2981.38–3057.88s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/458-the-ultimate-guide-to-the-titans-of-ul/)
- [Saturn Engine II](../components.md#unit-titans-cruiser2) **synergizes-with** [X-89 Bacterial Weapon Ω](../components.md#technology-x89). Cheap mobile cruiser fleets project force, while X-89 is proposed as a way to overcome opponents&#x27; greater ground-unit volume; this is a strategic complement, not a rules dependency. Sources: [SCPT 458, 8231.71–8315.41s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/458-the-ultimate-guide-to-the-titans-of-ul/)
- [Ul the Progenitor](../components.md#leader-titanshero) **enables** [Saturn Engine II](../components.md#unit-titans-cruiser2). The speakers recommend using the refreshed Elysium values for influence when tokens are the constraint, preserving resources for economical cruiser builds. Sources: [SCPT 458, 5452.74–5527.50s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/458-the-ultimate-guide-to-the-titans-of-ul/)
- [Hel-Titan I](../components.md#unit-titans-pds) **scores** [Build Defenses](../components.md#public-objective-build-defenses). Scattered Hel-Titans can make structure objectives easier to prepare for and score, subject to the objective&#x27;s actual requirements. Sources: [SCPT 458, 6170.16–6216.96s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/458-the-ultimate-guide-to-the-titans-of-ul/)

## Strategy claims

<a id="claim-c01"></a>

- **Draft:** Prioritize influence in the slice because command tokens fund the faction&#x27;s many activations, deployments, and fleet capacity; a low-influence/high-resource slice is a more serious constraint than the converse.
  Conditions: Draft/map dependent; the speakers prefer influence but say a 0/8 resources/influence slice is workable because Elysium can fund spending. Compatibility: SCPT 458, published 2026-05-27; guide mixes Prophecy of Kings-era advice and Thunders Edge-era discussion; not independently rules-verified. Uncertainty: Transcript misrecognizes several game terms; preference is strategic opinion, not a universal map rule.
  Sources: [SCPT 458 5727–5750s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/458-the-ultimate-guide-to-the-titans-of-ul/)
  Components: 
<a id="claim-c02"></a>

- **Draft:** Sell Terraform early when cash or an alliance changes the opening: the speakers set about three trade goods as a starting ask, adjust for the buyer, and value immediate money for technology, a Warfare build, or scoring above speculative later value.
  Conditions: Raise the price when an attachment objective or four-of-a-kind objective is visible; waiting can increase value, so price it against the table and the round-one need. Compatibility: SCPT 458 (2026-05-27); strategy discussion spans POK and Thunders Edge context; rules and current objective set not checked. Uncertainty: The three-trade-good baseline is one speaker&#x27;s negotiating heuristic; quotes vary with table wealth and buyer.
  Sources: [SCPT 458 3431–3478s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/458-the-ultimate-guide-to-the-titans-of-ul/)
  Components: [Terraform](../components.md#promissory-terraform)
<a id="claim-c03"></a>

- **Draft:** Consider trading Terraform for Research Agreement with Jol-Nar when the exchange gives Titans useful technology and Jol-Nar values the planet upgrade; Hyper Metabolism is singled out as attractive to Titans.
  Conditions: Only when the tech choice, timing, and mutual value are clear; the speakers call this one of the few swaps that can beat an early cash sale. Compatibility: SCPT 458 (2026-05-27), mixed-era strategic opinion; no current rules validation. Uncertainty: ASR renders some faction/tech names inconsistently; component ID for the named tech is unresolved in the assigned evidence, so no ID is asserted.
  Sources: [SCPT 458 3486–3511s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/458-the-ultimate-guide-to-the-titans-of-ul/)
  Components: [Terraform](../components.md#promissory-terraform), [Hyper Metabolism](../components.md#technology-hm)
<a id="claim-c04"></a>

- **Draft:** Use scan-link to explore only a planet where a Titans unit is already present when the system is activated; it yields one planet per activation, not every planet in a multi-planet system.
  Conditions: Pre-position a ship, Hel-Titan, or other qualifying unit on the planet before activating; do not count on a newly moved unit or sleeper placement to meet the prerequisite. Compatibility: SCPT 458 (2026-05-27), guide explanation; game-rule legality was not independently checked. Uncertainty: The audio/ASR calls it Scan Link / scan-link; source passage is clear about the existing-unit and one-planet constraints.
  Sources: [SCPT 458 1688–1728s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/458-the-ultimate-guide-to-the-titans-of-ul/)
  Components: [Scanlink Drone Network](../components.md#technology-sdn)
<a id="claim-c05"></a>

- **Draft:** Treat the activation sequence as separate timing windows: scan-link exploration happens on activation, Terragenesis can then place or move a sleeper after exploring, and Awaken can redeem only a sleeper already in the activated system before that activation.
  Conditions: Plan to explore/place now and Awaken on a later activation; a sleeper placed during the current activation cannot be redeemed by Awaken in that same action. Compatibility: SCPT 458 (2026-05-27); rules explanation in the guide is not an independent rules audit. Uncertainty: The speakers emphasize that wording is confusing; follow-up rules confirmation remains needed before treating as authoritative.
  Sources: [SCPT 458 2022–2095s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/458-the-ultimate-guide-to-the-titans-of-ul/) · [SCPT 458 2303–2310s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/458-the-ultimate-guide-to-the-titans-of-ul/)
  Components: [Terragenesis](../components.md#ability-terragenesis), [Awaken](../components.md#ability-awaken)
<a id="claim-c06"></a>

- **Draft:** Leave sleepers unredeemed when the threat of later Awaken/coalescence is more useful than an immediate Hel-Titan: opponents can see the token and must account for the possibility of Titans entering later.
  Conditions: Useful when preserving command tokens and creating deterrence or projection; limited by the five-token supply and opponents&#x27; willingness to avoid or challenge the location. Compatibility: SCPT 458 (2026-05-27); advice draws on a reported 2023 tournament game and POK-era faction play. Uncertainty: The discussion calls an unredeemed token nearly as useful, not strictly equivalent to a PDS; outcome depends on opponent behavior.
  Sources: [SCPT 458 2222–2266s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/458-the-ultimate-guide-to-the-titans-of-ul/)
  Components: [Coalescence](../components.md#ability-coalescence), [Awaken](../components.md#ability-awaken)
<a id="claim-c07"></a>

- **Draft:** Use coalescence as a projection and negotiation tool: when another player enters a sleeper location, Titans can awaken into the contested area and their units participate in the ensuing combat; the speakers now regard this as a central Titans skill.
  Conditions: Position sleepers where future access matters and budget for combat; do not treat dormant tokens as secret or as guaranteed ownership. Compatibility: SCPT 458 (2026-05-27), POK-era mechanic discussion; independent legality not checked. Uncertainty: The speakers revise an older dismissive view and report the tactic&#x27;s use becoming more common; their assessment is experience-based.
  Sources: [SCPT 458 2145–2197s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/458-the-ultimate-guide-to-the-titans-of-ul/) · [SCPT 458 2400–2404s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/458-the-ultimate-guide-to-the-titans-of-ul/)
  Components: [Coalescence](../components.md#ability-coalescence), [Awaken](../components.md#ability-awaken)
<a id="claim-c08"></a>

- **Draft:** Upgrade Saturn Engines early: Saturn Engine II is described as cost two, combat six, movement three, capacity two, and sustained damage, making it the core force-projection and combat upgrade.
  Conditions: Prioritize reaching the upgrade by round two when possible; choose a route that fits available skips, breakthrough, and strategy-card timing. Compatibility: SCPT 458 (2026-05-27), strategic evaluation; printed unit values and game legality not independently checked. Uncertainty: Speakers use strong superlatives, but note its fleet-pool footprint and that it is not superior in every niche (for example, it lacks bombardment).
  Sources: [SCPT 458 2565–2630s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/458-the-ultimate-guide-to-the-titans-of-ul/)
  Components: [Saturn Engine I](../components.md#unit-titans-cruiser), [Saturn Engine II](../components.md#unit-titans-cruiser2)
<a id="claim-c09"></a>

- **Draft:** Treat Saturn Engine II&#x27;s cheap movement and capacity as an all-purpose tool for objectives, raids, and fracture access, but account for each cruiser taking fleet capacity and for the limited number of command tokens.
  Conditions: Best when Titans can support several fleets and enough ground forces; opponents with much greater carrier capacity or ground-force volume can exploit the all-rounder&#x27;s limits. Compatibility: SCPT 458 (2026-05-27), strategic synthesis across the guide; no current-rules verification. Uncertainty: The speakers describe the ship as versatile rather than best-in-class at every task.
  Sources: [SCPT 458 6090–6110s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/458-the-ultimate-guide-to-the-titans-of-ul/) · [SCPT 458 6308–6333s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/458-the-ultimate-guide-to-the-titans-of-ul/) · [SCPT 458 8244–8306s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/458-the-ultimate-guide-to-the-titans-of-ul/)
  Components: [Saturn Engine II](../components.md#unit-titans-cruiser2)
<a id="claim-c10"></a>

- **Draft:** Spread Hel-Titans across planets to project durable ground defense and production instead of concentrating several on one planet; one per planet usually covers more ground and keeps structure objectives accessible.
  Conditions: Multiple Hel-Titans in one system can still be useful for production; concentrate only when the objective or defense position justifies it. Compatibility: SCPT 458 (2026-05-27), guide strategy opinion; current unit rules not checked. Uncertainty: The source gives a general preference, not a strict threshold or universal optimum.
  Sources: [SCPT 458 2482–2495s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/458-the-ultimate-guide-to-the-titans-of-ul/) · [SCPT 458 3123–3182s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/458-the-ultimate-guide-to-the-titans-of-ul/)
  Components: [Hel-Titan I](../components.md#unit-titans-pds)
<a id="claim-c11"></a>

- **Draft:** Keep at least one Hecatoncheires in reinforcements when possible, because its deploy ability converts a PDS placement into a mech plus infantry; using Transit Diodes to remove and replace a PDS can create this deployment opportunity elsewhere.
  Conditions: Check that a mech remains in reinforcements and that the placement effect qualifies; do not fill all mech slots early if a later deployment is valuable. Compatibility: SCPT 458 (2026-05-27), guide discussion of POK components and interaction; not independently rules-verified. Uncertainty: The speakers call this a rules-nerdy interaction and caution that other effects that merely move ground forces do not move Hel-Titans.
  Sources: [SCPT 458 3024–3043s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/458-the-ultimate-guide-to-the-titans-of-ul/) · [SCPT 458 3076–3085s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/458-the-ultimate-guide-to-the-titans-of-ul/) · [SCPT 458 3161–3186s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/458-the-ultimate-guide-to-the-titans-of-ul/)
  Components: [Hecatoncheires](../components.md#unit-titans-mech), [Transit Diodes](../components.md#technology-td), [Hel-Titan I](../components.md#unit-titans-pds)
<a id="claim-c12"></a>

- **Draft:** The speakers favor spending Elysium for influence more often than its seven resources after the hero refresh, because Titans&#x27; binding shortage is command tokens rather than unit cost.
  Conditions: Choose resources when a specific spend objective or double-tech plan warrants it; the preference assumes Saturn Engine II remains the efficient fleet backbone. Compatibility: SCPT 458 (2026-05-27); hero text and economic evaluation not independently checked. Uncertainty: The speakers disagree in emphasis and one calls the seven-resource use a trap; treat this as situational advice.
  Sources: [SCPT 458 5453–5528s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/458-the-ultimate-guide-to-the-titans-of-ul/)
